A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same filter-normalization study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the appendix and main text.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification and robustness experiments on CIFAR-10, ImageNet, ExDark, and LEGUS, together with original appendix experiments and analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and the appendices, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and diagnostic analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains separate normalization of positive and negative filter weights, numerical stabilization, and learnable scaling and shifting. No proposed algorithm component or model procedure changes.

E1.justification: Dataset and task coverage is retained, including artificial atmospheric corruptions, natural low-light and astronomy data, and ImageNet-C/P evaluations. The nine-bin ImageNet contrast evaluation in v5 already appears in v3 Appendix A.7.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same ResNet, ViT, CLIP, normalization-equivariant, normalization-layer, and soft-regularization comparators. No evaluated comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: The stated training settings, corruption definitions, evaluation metrics, and sample-selection procedures are unchanged. Figure 13 still examines each filter's 100 highest-response images from DC; changing its horizontal display from rank to absolute weight ratio does not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: The existing first-layer error analysis in Section 4.3/Figure 13 is revised with different per-filter error observations and a redrawn fitted curve. Other ablations and robustness analyses are retained; the contrast-bin analysis is relocated rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: There are no additions or removals of repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests. Statistical reporting conventions remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 13's right panel contains changed error-count observations, beyond its axis revision: the highest R34N point changes from approximately 39 to 48 errors among 100 images. The qualitative finding is retained. Tabulated benchmark results are unchanged, including v3 Table A9, reproduced as v5 Table 2.

T1.justification: The positive-weight-ratio definition, filter decomposition, and gain/offset equivariance derivations in Section 3 are unchanged. Appendix A.5 also retains the same soft-regularization formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and summary retain the same contributions: filter normalization for atmospheric equivariance, improved robustness and generalization, more diverse filters, and advantages over larger comparison models.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning filter diversity, misclassification, nonlinearities, and applicability to atmospheric transformations are retained. The main-text interpretation of contrast-bin robustness restates the existing discussion in v3 Appendix A.7.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hyperparameters, hardware/timing specifications, and code-access information are unchanged. The added NAIRR compute-support acknowledgment supplies no new hardware configuration or experimental instructions.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 41 references and the same positioning relative to equivariant networks, activation normalization, data augmentation, and vision architectures.

P1.justification: The contrast-analysis paragraph moves from Appendix A.7 to Section 4.1 with limited rewriting. Figure 13's explanatory wording is adjusted, the publication footer changes to NeurIPS 2025, and the acknowledgments add compute support.

P2.justification: Appendix Table A9 becomes main-text Table 2 with new example-image panels illustrating low, middle, and high contrast. Figure 13 replaces filter ranks with absolute weight ratios and redraws its curves and legend. The final appendix figure is relocated, while most displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v5 makes existing evidence easier to assess by illustrating contrast bins in main-text Table 2 and plotting errors directly against absolute weight ratio in Figure 13. These provide a modest clarity improvement. The revised diagnostic observations retain the earlier qualitative conclusion, while the method and benchmark results remain unchanged.
